entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A black body at the 2,350 K dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Deming et al. 2023, dayside brightness temperature at 3.6 µm (uniform reanalysis of Spitzer's eclipses, CDS J/AJ/165/104 table 2)): #ff9d3d. Chosen from the archive's emission rows by rule: 2 measured of 2 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength. Reflected starlight is not included.

entries.subject: Jansen & Kipping (2020)'s TESS phase-curve fit as a temperature map
entries.finding: Included on 2026-10-15 as the TESS dataset, the default. Their thermal component is Cowan & Agol (2011)'s energy-balance map with fitted A_B 0.24, epsilon 10.9 and f 1.22 (results table) for T_eff 6940 K and a/R_star 5.464 from rho_star and P (parameter table, which these reproduce as T_eq 2099 K). Drawn as printed, the equator runs from 2707 to 2370 K, within the printed T_max 2710 +/- 100 and T_min 2380 +170/-200 K; its hottest longitude, 66 degrees east, is 1 degree short of the printed 71 +2/-4, a median over the fit's samples rather than the map of the median parameters. The map's shape is the model's, TESS sees reflected light too, which the same model separates.
